title: Bharti Airtel, Trent, SBI Among 215 Stocks to Report Q1 Results This Week
excerpt: India's busiest earnings week of the season features heavyweights across telecom, real estate, retail, and banking, with multiple sectors expected to show profit declines.
body:
• Over 215 companies will report April-June quarter results this week, making it the busiest earnings period of the season
  • Key names include Bharti Airtel (Monday), DLF (Monday), Trent and Bajaj Auto (Wednesday), Titan and LIC (Thursday), and SBI and Tata Motors (Friday)
  • Analysts expect double-digit profit declines across oil and gas, cement, chemicals, and select telecom names
  • Largecap earnings growth is forecast to slow to around 7% year-on-year, the weakest in several quarters

A Packed Calendar

Indian markets enter the heaviest earnings week of the Q1 FY27 season starting Monday, with more than 215 listed companies scheduled to report results for the quarter ended June 2026. The lineup spans every major sector and includes several Nifty 50 constituents whose numbers will set the tone for the index through August.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=cSkNwiFBr2A

Monday opens with Bharti Airtel — India's largest private telecom operator — alongside real estate bellwether DLF, Shree Cements, Marico, Aurobindo Pharma, and Bosch. Airtel's Q1 FY27 numbers will be closely watched after the company delivered a blockbuster Q1 FY26, when revenue jumped 28.5% and profit more than doubled to Rs 5,948 crore.

Day-by-Day Highlights

Monday (August 4): Bharti Airtel, DLF, Siemens Energy India, Shree Cements, Bosch, Marico, Aditya Birla Capital, Aurobindo Pharma, Ather Energy, and Kansai Nerolac Paints.

"Sector Pressure Points Brokerage Motilal Oswal has flagged that largecap earnings growth could slow to roughly 7% year-on-year this quarter — the weakest pace in recent memory."

Tuesday (August 5): Britannia Industries, Adani Ports, Lupin, Bharti Hexacom, Berger Paints, Container Corporation of India, Torrent Power, Exide Industries, and Gujarat Gas.

Wednesday (August 6): Trent, Bajaj Auto, Divi's Laboratories, Power Finance Corporation, Pidilite Industries, BHEL, Hero MotoCorp, Jindal Stainless, and PVR Inox.

Thursday (August 7): Titan Company, Life Insurance Corporation, Cummins India, HPCL, BSE, Kalyan Jewellers, Page Industries, Biocon, and Linde India.

Friday (August 8): State Bank of India, Tata Motors, Info Edge, Grasim Industries, and Garden Reach Shipbuilders.

Sector Pressure Points

Brokerage Motilal Oswal has flagged that largecap earnings growth could slow to roughly 7% year-on-year this quarter — the weakest pace in recent memory. The drag is concentrated in specific pockets.

Oil and gas names face some of the steepest declines. GAIL's profit is expected to fall 49%, Gujarat Gas by 97%, HPCL by 31%, and Mahanagar Gas by 66%. Real estate is also under pressure, with DLF projected to report a 17% profit decline.

In telecom, Bharti Airtel's profit may drop around 31% on a year-on-year basis despite continued subscriber and ARPU gains, owing to higher depreciation and finance costs. Cement companies — Ambuja Cements, ACC, Dalmia Bharat, and Shree Cements — are collectively expected to show mid-teens to high-30s profit declines as pricing power remains weak.

The chemicals sector offers no relief either. Clean Science may see a 43% profit fall, Deepak Nitrite 27%, and PI Industries 19%.

Bright Spots to Watch

Not everything is bearish. Select consumer-facing names and banks with strong retail franchises could deliver positive surprises. Bajaj Auto, riding strong export demand, and Titan, benefiting from elevated gold prices, are among the few names where expectations are more constructive.

Trent's results on Wednesday will be watched for signs of whether the Zudio-driven growth engine is sustaining its pace or showing fatigue after the stock's steep run-up.

Market Impact

With the Nifty 50 trading near the 24,500 level, this week's earnings will determine whether the index can sustain its recent momentum or faces a reset. For investors, the sheer volume of results means sector-level patterns will matter more than individual surprises — and the pattern so far points to a quarter where topline resilience has not translated into bottom-line growth.
